rows.practice: gathers market, accounting and household data, runs simple statistical tests in software and applies valuation and portfolio tools to real financial problems
rows.knowledge: core finance theory such as arbitrage, asset pricing and cost of capital, how markets are regulated and how fintech and climate risk reshape financial services
rows.identity: a finance student who weighs governance and ethics in every financial decision and sees finance as a lever for sustainable outcomes for people and planet

rows.practice: investigates complex finance problems with largely autonomous judgement, chooses and justifies established methods and defends decisions with well-evidenced, original argument
rows.knowledge: rigorous command of finance paradigms and methods, deep knowledge of several specialist areas and a keen sense of the uncertainty and limits in financial evidence
rows.identity: an independent financial analyst who reads well past taught material, questions every source critically and takes ownership of decisions on complex problems (ing's reading)

rows.practice: conducts a self-directed dissertation or applied project, ideally testing a financial question empirically against data, after deeper taught study of core specialisms
rows.knowledge: advanced specialist knowledge in one or more core areas of finance and the research methods that underpin empirical testing of financial theory
rows.identity: an emerging finance researcher or specialist who treats research as central to practice and may go on to doctoral study (ing's reading)

digest.definition: Finance studies national and international financial markets and how they interact with households, firms, the third sector, institutions and governments; it is global, central to decisions and always changing
distinctiveFeatures: Finance studies national and international financial markets and how they interact with households, firms, the third sector, institutions and governments; it is global, central to decisions and always changing
It joins conceptual study, the theory, with applied study, empirical methods and theory in practice, and keeps both in balance, also in joint degrees

Two core domains: markets, banks and institutions; and investment, value, corporate finance, securities, risk and international financial management, with newer areas such as sustainable finance, fintech and AI
It is approached from behavioural, ethical, economic, sustainable and statistical or mathematical angles, with the ethical and social side always present
It draws on accounting and economics but needs only a reasonable knowledge of accounting
It is data driven: statistical and econometric work, programming and AI tools are part of the degree
Professional bodies give advanced standing and accreditation, especially for specialist master's courses

employability through trading simulations, investment competitions, placements, guest practitioners and incubators; transferable skills sought by the finance sector (D1, 1.37 to 1.42)

subjectSpecific.text: You are expected to understand the settings finance works in, from law and regulation to tax, and how they shape markets and institutions.
You are expected to know the main theories and tools of finance, such as portfolio theory and asset pricing, and how to use them on real problems.
You are expected to understand how finance theories are tested against data, and to weigh up the evidence in at least one area while seeing its limits.
You are expected to read and analyse financial data with spreadsheets or statistical software, and to question your results and the assumptions behind them.
You are expected to understand how organisations raise money and are governed, and to judge how well those arrangements work.
You are expected to understand what shapes how people save, invest and manage money, from risk attitudes to pensions and tax.
You are expected to understand how financial services such as banking, insurance and pensions work and change, and how theory helps explain them.
You are expected to read financial statements and see where reporting and disclosure can mislead or leave gaps.
You are expected to understand why finance is regulated, what rules firms and markets face and what that means for how you work as a professional.
You are expected to judge how digital technology, AI and generative AI are changing financial services, markets and investment.
You are expected to understand personal finance, how people become financially capable, and why wider access to finance matters.
You are expected to understand how finance responds to climate change and environmental risk, and how green and sustainable finance products work.
You are expected to use programming, data visualisation and AI tools on real data, and to choose the right research methods for the data you have.

transferable.text: You are expected to weigh up arguments and evidence critically.
You are expected to learn on your own initiative and manage your own study.
You are expected to analyse and sift data, whether given or gathered yourself, and reach reasoned conclusions, mostly on well-defined problems.
You are expected to find, extract and manage data from different sources and reference them properly.
You are expected to be confident with numbers, analysing financial data and understanding the statistics behind it.
You are expected to choose and use research tools to shape and interpret policies in finance, society and the environment.
You are expected to use technology to gather, analyse and share financial information.
You are expected to present numbers and ideas, with your analysis and argument, in a way that suits your audience, in speech and in writing.
You are expected to work well with others, for example on group projects.

statements.about: joint degrees read with the partner subject's statement
statements.paraphrase: Where Finance is one half of a joint degree, the statement should be read together with the statements for the other discipline, keeping the balance of theory and application intact.

forPractitioner.text: For a joint or combined award, read this statement alongside the partner subject's statement, and check that the Finance part keeps its scope, depth and balance of theory and practice.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design joint courses

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Finance degree

statements.about: fundamentals and new developments in theory and practice
statements.paraphrase: A Finance degree aims to help students understand what finance does in business and organisations, as a base for many careers; it requires study of both the foundations and the newest work in finance theory and practice.

forPractitioner.text: Build the curriculum so that students study both the established foundations and current advances in finance theory and practice, organised around two main subject domains.

forBeneficiary.text: Studying finance means learning both its established foundations and its newest ideas, in theory and in practice, so that you understand what finance does in organisations.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Finance degree

statements.about: the two core domains and contemporary areas
statements.paraphrase: Students must understand two domains: how markets, banks, exchanges and institutions are designed and work, with the roles of governments and individuals; and investment, value, corporate finance, securities analysis, risk and international financial management. They are also expected to understand newer areas such as climate and sustainable finance, fintech, AI and data analytics, alternative investments and global uncertainty.

forPractitioner.text: Cover both core domains, financial markets and institutions, and investment and corporate finance, and add contemporary areas such as sustainable finance, fintech, AI and alternative investments; the newer areas are expected, the core domains required.

forBeneficiary.text: You will need to understand how financial markets and institutions work and the principles of investment, value, corporate finance and risk; you are also expected to understand newer areas such as sustainable finance, fintech and AI.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Finance degree

statements.about: awareness of the ethical and social side of finance
statements.paraphrase: Finance can be studied from behavioural, ethical, economic, sustainable and statistical angles; students will at least become conscious of the ethical and social sides of financial activity and systems, as well as the economic ones.

forPractitioner.text: Whatever the angle a course takes, make sure every student will come away conscious of the ethical and social sides of financial activity, not only the economic one.

forBeneficiary.text: Whatever your route through the subject, you will become aware of the ethical and social side of financial activity and systems, not only the economics.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Finance degree

statements.about: specialist master's judged against the highest levels
statements.paraphrase: Specialist master's courses go deeper into one or more core bachelor's components and may add related specialisms; they would be expected to be judged against the statement's highest levels of achievement plus content criteria for their focus, and usually admit holders of at least a second-class Finance degree.

forPractitioner.text: Judge a specialist master's in Finance against the excellent level (4.6) and against extra content criteria for its specialism; entry is usually a second-class Finance honours degree or above.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a statement about how a course is evaluated and who it admits

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree

statements.about: EDI embedded in the culture and practice of Finance
statements.paraphrase: Equality, diversity and inclusion take in many identity characteristics and their intersections; EDI should be built meaningfully into the culture and practice of the discipline and every Finance course, which also reflect industry EDI codes where suitable.

forPractitioner.text: Embed EDI meaningfully in the culture, practice and curriculum of every Finance course, and refer to industry EDI codes where they apply.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and the discipline

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree

statements.about: an environment where every student can thrive
statements.paraphrase: Students from varied backgrounds come to Finance; whatever the combination taught, those who teach it must create an environment in which all students can thrive and feel represented and included, starting with widening participation.

forPractitioner.text: Create a learning environment where every student can thrive and feels represented and included, and support widening participation to limit the effect of economic disadvantage.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who teach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree

statements.paraphrase: Teaching and assessment in Finance should reflect EDI principles; varied teaching modes can be used, and assessment should be as inclusive as possible, for instance by offering alternative types, timings or modes where suitable.

forPractitioner.text: Design assessment to be as inclusive as possible: offer alternatives in type, duration and mode where suitable, such as a written task for a presentation or extra exam time.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course; a student meets its effect as alternative assessment

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree

statements.paraphrase: Physical and online learning environments must be adaptable and mirror the diversity of the students.

forPractitioner.text: Make physical and virtual learning spaces flexible and reflective of the students who use them.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its spaces

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree

statements.paraphrase: Teaching and assessment materials, readings and case studies included, should carry varied perspectives so that no student's background puts them at a disadvantage.

forPractitioner.text: Choose readings, cases and assessment materials that carry varied perspectives, so that no student is disadvantaged by background.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who choose materials

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree

statements.about: the hidden curriculum and the language of finance
statements.paraphrase: The hidden curriculum needs attention, above all the specialist language of finance, so that it does not get in the way of learning.

forPractitioner.text: Attend to the hidden curriculum, especially the jargon of finance, so that unspoken expectations and terms do not block learning.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who teach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree

statements.about: equal access to placements and visits
statements.paraphrase: Where a Finance course offers a placement, work experience or industry visit, equality of access for all students must be considered.

forPractitioner.text: When you offer placements, work experience or industry visits, consider whether every student can take them up on equal terms.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree

statements.paraphrase: Finance courses should monitor and review EDI to see how well current policies work and how to improve them.

forPractitioner.text: Monitor and review how well your EDI policies are working in the programme, and plan improvements.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course

Accessibility and the needs of disabled students

statements.about: accessibility at every stage, regulatory minimum
statements.paraphrase: Accessibility means removing barriers so that learners can reach outcomes fairly; it should at least meet regulatory requirements and will apply at every stage, from pre-application information to graduation and after.

forPractitioner.text: Meet the regulatory requirements for accessibility as a minimum and apply them at every stage, from pre-application information to after graduation; draw on institutional guidance and support.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course; a student meets its effect

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree
Accessibility and the needs of disabled students

statements.paraphrase: Databases, simulation tools and software should be usable by every student, for example through remote access or quiet spaces; accessibility counts when choosing them, and class materials take account of the hidden curriculum.

forPractitioner.text: Make databases, trading simulations and software accessible to all, for example by remote access or low-stimulation spaces, and weigh accessibility when you choose them.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its resources

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree
Accessibility and the needs of disabled students

statements.about: the same opportunities for every student
statements.paraphrase: Placements, internships, international learning and extracurricular activities should be open to every student whatever their background, disability or other protected characteristic.

forPractitioner.text: Open placements, internships, international and extracurricular opportunities to every student on equal terms.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree
Accessibility and the needs of disabled students

statements.paraphrase: Courses should take account of what keeps students from attending or achieving, such as caring duties and digital poverty, and act where they can to reduce it.

forPractitioner.text: Identify barriers such as caring responsibilities and digital poverty and take what steps you can to reduce their effect on learning.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree
Accessibility and the needs of disabled students

statements.paraphrase: Assessment in Finance should take accessibility into account; outcomes can often be shown another way through alternative assessment.

forPractitioner.text: Check each assessment for accessibility and, where needed, let students show the same outcome another way.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on assessment design

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree
Accessibility and the needs of disabled students

statements.paraphrase: Courses should consider universal design for learning and build choice of assessment into Finance programmes.

forPractitioner.text: Consider universal design for learning and build assessment choice into the programme.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree
Accessibility and the needs of disabled students

statements.about: proactive inclusive design for neurodivergent students
statements.paraphrase: Learning, teaching and assessment should be designed ahead of time to include everyone and to avoid barriers for neurodivergent students and those with specific learning difficulties.

forPractitioner.text: Design learning, teaching and assessment in advance to include neurodivergent students and those with specific learning difficulties, rather than adjusting later.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree

statements.about: sustainable solutions as part of wider efforts
statements.paraphrase: Finance degrees aim to equip students to devise sustainable solutions for a stable financial system; these should be seen as one part of efforts across disciplines on climate, nature, pollution, inequality and uncertainty, which call for critical and creative skills that cross subject boundaries.

forPractitioner.text: Teach sustainable financial solutions as one part of work across disciplines on climate, nature loss and inequality, and build the critical and creative skills that cross subject lines.

forBeneficiary.text: You should see the sustainable solutions you work on in finance as one part of a wider effort across many disciplines, and build critical and creative skills that cross subject lines.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree

statements.about: competencies for sustainable decisions and disclosure
statements.paraphrase: The core skills of Finance degrees match the ESD guidance's outcomes, among them systems, anticipatory, strategic and critical thinking and integrated problem-solving; Finance degrees should develop capacities that put sustainable decisions and disclosure first.

forPractitioner.text: Develop capacities and competencies that put sustainable decision making and disclosure first, using the ESD guidance's competencies as a reference.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design; the student-facing outcome is 4.4.b11

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Finance degree

statements.about: the wider context of finance skills
statements.paraphrase: Entrepreneurship education helps students build a rewarding, self-directed working life that adds social, cultural and economic value; Finance graduates should appreciate the wider setting in which they apply their skills, including sustainability, climate finance and nature and biodiversity finance.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates should appreciate where their skills are used, including sustainability, climate finance and biodiversity finance; build this into enterprise education.

forBeneficiary.text: You should come to appreciate the wider setting for your finance skills, including sustainability, climate finance and finance for nature and biodiversity.

headingPath: Distinctive features of the Finance degree

statements.about: critical thinking and the ethical and regulatory side of finance
statements.paraphrase: Finance courses align learning objectives with section 4 and should be designed so that students can build critical thinking and apply judgement to finance problems; design flexibility is needed for AI, fintech and digital assets, and students should be able to judge the ethical, sustainability and regulatory sides of financial activity, not only how institutions work or how products are priced.

forPractitioner.text: Design objectives that integrate concept and application and let students develop critical thinking and judgement; students should be able to evaluate the ethical, sustainability and regulatory dimensions of finance, beyond pricing and functions.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to judge the ethical, sustainability and regulatory side of financial activity, not only how institutions work or how products are priced, and use critical thinking on finance problems.

headingPath: Distinctive features of the Finance degree

statements.paraphrase: Deep accounting knowledge is not required, but a reasonable knowledge of accounting principles, the regulation of financial reporting, what financial statements contain and how accounting information informs decisions is required; joint degrees with Finance include most of the statement's knowledge and skills.

forPractitioner.text: Teach enough accounting for a reasonable command of its principles, financial reporting regulation, the content of financial statements and using accounting information for decisions; depth beyond that depends on the programme.

forBeneficiary.text: You do not need deep accounting, but you are required to know the principles of accounting, how financial reporting is regulated, what financial statements contain and how accounting information supports decisions.

headingPath: Distinctive features of the Finance degree

statements.about: lifelong learning and a range of careers
statements.paraphrase: Finance courses should ready students for self-directed learning throughout life and be designed so that they can flourish in many finance careers across sectors, in enterprise or in further study.

forPractitioner.text: Design the programme to prepare students for self-directed, lifelong learning and for careers across public, private and third sectors, enterprise or further study.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design

headingPath: Distinctive features of the Finance degree

statements.about: core skills in a joint degree
statements.paraphrase: Undergraduates taking Finance within a joint or combined degree will achieve the core of the specific and generic skills in the statement, add others from their other subject and may explore where the disciplines overlap.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure joint and combined students will achieve the core specific and generic skills, then add the other subject's skills and room for interdisciplinary work.

forBeneficiary.text: If you study finance as part of a joint degree, you will gain its core subject and general skills, add skills from your other subject and can explore where the two meet.

headingPath: Distinctive features of the Finance degree

statements.about: the master's project or dissertation and empirical work
statements.paraphrase: A full master's usually carries 180 credits over one full-time year; after the taught part, students normally complete a self-directed project or dissertation that ideally should include empirical work, though applied projects or extra taught units may take its place.

forPractitioner.text: Plan the master's around about 180 credits with a self-directed project or dissertation that ideally should include empirical work; live briefs, internships or extra taught units are accepted variants.

forBeneficiary.text: On a full master's you will usually finish with your own project or dissertation, ideally one that should include empirical work you carry out yourself.

headingPath: Distinctive features of the Finance degree

statements.about: research as part of master's education
statements.paraphrase: Master's students should be taught with research in mind as an important part of their study, since some will go on to further study.

forPractitioner.text: Treat research as a central part of master's teaching, since some students will continue to doctoral study.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on how the course is taught

headingPath: Distinctive features of the Finance degree

statements.paraphrase: Courses support learning and are inclusive; Finance degrees should be offered in several modes with assessment that suits students' needs, which may include on-campus, online, hybrid, block or part-time study and credit from micro-credentials or prior learning.

forPractitioner.text: Offer the degree in a variety of learning modes, with assessment suited to students' needs, and consider credit routes such as micro-credentials and recognition of prior learning.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on how the course is offered

headingPath: Distinctive features of the Finance degree

statements.about: flexibility kept coherent and on standard
statements.paraphrase: When flexibility is built into Finance degrees, it is essential that programmes stay coherent and meet the statement's standards; flexibility may be needed to meet EDI obligations, and partnerships can add more.

forPractitioner.text: However flexible the structure, keep the programme coherent and meeting this statement's standards; flexibility may also be how you meet EDI obligations.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design

statements.paraphrase: A grasp of the settings finance works in, with knowledge of the institutional framework needed to understand how markets and institutions function, such as economic, ethical, legal, political, regulatory, social and tax settings.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to know the economic, legal, regulatory, social and tax settings of finance and the institutional framework of markets and firms.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to understand the settings finance works in, from law and regulation to tax, and how they shape markets and institutions.

statements.about: major theories and tools of finance
statements.paraphrase: Knowledge of finance's main theoretical tools and theories and how they bear on theoretical and practical problems, for example arbitrage, portfolio theory, asset pricing, cost of capital, derivatives, behavioural finance and climate finance.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to know the main theories and tools of finance and how to apply them to theoretical and practical problems.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to know the main theories and tools of finance, such as portfolio theory and asset pricing, and how to use them on real problems.

statements.paraphrase: An understanding of how finance theory relates to empirical testing, used to appraise the evidence in at least one major area, recognising how tests and theory are limited and change over time.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to relate finance theory to empirical tests and to appraise the evidence in at least one major area, aware of its limits.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to understand how finance theories are tested against data, and to weigh up the evidence in at least one area while seeing its limits.

statements.paraphrase: An ability to interpret financial data from firms, households, national sources and markets, analysing it with statistical tools in spreadsheets or econometric software, possibly running statistical and econometric tests, and critiquing results and their assumptions.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to interpret and analyse financial data with spreadsheets and statistical software, and to critique the results and their assumptions.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to read and analyse financial data with spreadsheets or statistical software, and to question your results and the assumptions behind them.

statements.paraphrase: An understanding of how firms and other organisations are financed and governed, and how theory and evidence together can judge whether those arrangements are effective and efficient.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to understand financing and governance structures and to judge their effectiveness using theory and evidence.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to understand how organisations raise money and are governed, and to judge how well those arrangements work.

statements.paraphrase: An understanding of what shapes how individuals manage money and invest, and the opportunities open to them, such as risk attitudes, portfolio choice, pensions, tax on savings and currency risk.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to understand what drives the financial and investment behaviour of individuals and their options.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to understand what shapes how people save, invest and manage money, from risk attitudes to pensions and tax.

statements.paraphrase: An understanding of financial service activity in the economy and what changes it, and of how theory and evidence, such as information asymmetry or market efficiency, help explain it.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to understand financial services and their change over time, using theory and evidence to explain them.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to understand how financial services such as banking, insurance and pensions work and change, and how theory helps explain them.

statements.paraphrase: Able to read financial statements, with a fair awareness of where financial reporting and disclosure fall short, for example accrual versus cash accounting and discretionary practices.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to read financial statements and to recognise the limits of reporting and disclosure.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to read financial statements and see where reporting and disclosure can mislead or leave gaps.

statements.paraphrase: An understanding of how regulation in finance is organised, why it exists, what it asks of firms and markets, how it differs across industries and economies, and what it means for practitioners' professionalism.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to understand the reasons for, reach and effect of financial regulation and its implications for professional practice.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to understand why finance is regulated, what rules firms and markets face and what that means for how you work as a professional.

statements.about: technology, AI and GenAI in finance
statements.paraphrase: An ability to judge how technologies, including digital tools, AI and GenAI, make new ways of delivering financial services possible and affect markets and investment, in areas such as payments, lending, fraud detection and compliance.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to assess the role of digital technology, AI and GenAI in financial services, markets and investment.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to judge how digital technology, AI and generative AI are changing financial services, markets and investment.

statements.paraphrase: An ability to understand personal finance and see how financial literacy and capability are built, and to value widening access to finance through mainstream and alternative channels.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to understand personal finance and financial capability and to value wider access to finance.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to understand personal finance, how people become financially capable, and why wider access to finance matters.

statements.about: finance and climate and environmental risk
statements.paraphrase: An ability to understand what the finance sector does about climate change and other environmental risks, and how green and climate finance, nature and biodiversity finance and sustainable products have grown.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to understand finance's role in climate and environmental risk and the growth of green and sustainable finance.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to understand how finance responds to climate change and environmental risk, and how green and sustainable finance products work.

statements.paraphrase: Knowledge of the programming, data visualisation, AI and computing skills the profession needs, the ability to apply them to real data in statistical or econometric software, and a grasp of quantitative and qualitative data with the choice of fitting research methods.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to use programming, visualisation and AI tools on real data and to choose suitable quantitative or qualitative methods.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to use programming, data visualisation and AI tools on real data, and to choose the right research methods for the data you have.

statements.paraphrase: Weighing arguments and evidence critically.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to evaluate arguments and evidence critically.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to weigh up arguments and evidence critically.

statements.paraphrase: Learning on one's own initiative and managing one's own study.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to learn independently and manage their own learning.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to learn on your own initiative and manage your own study.

statements.paraphrase: Analysing, filtering and judging data, and drawing reasoned conclusions about structured and, to a lesser degree, unstructured problems from given data or data the student gathers.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to analyse and filter data and reach reasoned conclusions on structured and some unstructured problems.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to analyse and sift data, whether given or gathered yourself, and reach reasoned conclusions, mostly on well-defined problems.

statements.about: finding and managing data from many sources
statements.paraphrase: Locating, extracting, managing and analysing data from several sources, acknowledging and referencing them.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to locate, extract, manage and analyse data from several sources, with proper referencing.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to find, extract and manage data from different sources and reference them properly.

statements.paraphrase: Numeracy, including handling and analysing financial and other numbers and grasping statistical and econometric ideas at a suitable level.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to be numerate, processing financial data and grasping statistical and econometric concepts.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to be confident with numbers, analysing financial data and understanding the statistics behind it.

statements.paraphrase: Choosing and using research tools to design, steer and interpret financial, social and environmental policy.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to select and apply research tools to design and interpret financial, social and environmental policies.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to choose and use research tools to shape and interpret policies in finance, society and the environment.

statements.paraphrase: Using technology to gather, analyse and communicate financial information.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to use technology to acquire, analyse and communicate financial information.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to use technology to gather, analyse and share financial information.

statements.paraphrase: Communicating quantitative and qualitative information with analysis and argument in a form suited to the audience, spoken, non-verbal and written.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to communicate numerical and qualitative analysis and argument in forms that suit the audience.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to present numbers and ideas, with your analysis and argument, in a way that suits your audience, in speech and in writing.

statements.paraphrase: Working with others, for instance in group projects.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates are generally expected to work well with others, for example in group projects.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to work well with others, for example on group projects.

statements.about: the provider's choice of activities and showing they work
statements.paraphrase: Each provider is responsible for choosing teaching, learning and assessment suited to its degree's aims, and will be able to show how those activities let students reach the subject knowledge and skills and the generic skills in section 3.

forPractitioner.text: Choose your own mix of teaching, learning and assessment, and be ready to show how it enables students to reach the outcomes in 3.2 and 3.3.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider

statements.paraphrase: Blended delivery mixing online and in-person work can be used and adds flexibility but can weaken engagement; learning and assessment supported by technology needs fresh approaches that also address integrity, and blended learning must maintain academic integrity.

forPractitioner.text: If you use blended learning, keep students engaged and make sure the approach maintains academic integrity, designing technology-supported assessment with integrity in mind.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course delivery

statements.about: support for language, mathematics, writing and study skills
statements.paraphrase: Finance students at both levels often come from varied backgrounds; programme directors and course leaders should consider targeted help with subject language, mathematics where needed, academic writing and study and exam skills.

forPractitioner.text: Consider targeted support in subject-specific language, mathematics where relevant, academic writing and study and examination skills for a diverse cohort.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on programme leaders; a student meets its effect as support

statements.paraphrase: Teaching and assessment design can draw on current pedagogical research and technology; regular reviews must be carried out so that the activities stay fit for purpose and current for the programme's outcomes.

forPractitioner.text: Review teaching, learning and assessment regularly so that it stays fit for purpose and current, drawing on pedagogical research and new technology.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course

statements.about: Annex D for evidence of achievement
statements.paraphrase: Most students are likely to go well beyond the threshold; each provider sets how to evidence achievement and should consult Annex D of the Frameworks for more guidance.

forPractitioner.text: Decide what evidence shows achievement at each level and use Annex D, the degree classification descriptions, as your guide.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in judging achievement

statements.about: competence standards and Equality Act guidance
statements.paraphrase: The three levels are not universal competence standards; a provider that sets competence standards under the Equality Act 2010 may draw on the statement and PSRB requirements, and should follow the latest guidance from the Equality and Human Rights Commission.

forPractitioner.text: Do not treat the threshold, typical and excellent levels as competence standards; if you write competence standards under the Equality Act 2010, follow the EHRC's latest guidance.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider

statements.about: depth of knowledge of core concepts
statements.paraphrase: Will show a depth of knowledge of finance's main concepts, theories and tools.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will show deep knowledge of finance's main concepts, theories and tools.

forBeneficiary.text: To pass, you will show solid knowledge of the main ideas, theories and tools of finance.

statements.paraphrase: Will apply what they know to finance problems that matter to people, firms, institutions and society.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will apply their knowledge to finance problems facing individuals, companies, institutions and society.

forBeneficiary.text: To pass, you will use what you know to tackle finance problems for people, firms, institutions and society.

statements.paraphrase: Will show they understand the settings of finance: institutional, economic, political, regulatory and social.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will understand the institutional, economic, political, regulatory and social environments of finance.

forBeneficiary.text: To pass, you will understand the institutions, economics, politics, regulation and society that finance works within.

statements.paraphrase: Will recognise how much sound governance and ethics matter in financial decisions.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will recognise that reliable governance and ethical considerations are fundamental to financial decisions.

forBeneficiary.text: To pass, you will recognise why good governance and ethics matter in financial decisions.

statements.paraphrase: Will understand how financial markets work and are regulated and supervised, with some of what they trade.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will understand how financial markets operate and are regulated and supervised, with some of their products.

forBeneficiary.text: To pass, you will understand how financial markets work and are regulated, and some of the products traded in them.

statements.paraphrase: Will understand the basics of valuing assets, analysing securities and managing portfolios.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will understand the basics of valuation, security analysis and portfolio management.

forBeneficiary.text: To pass, you will understand the basics of valuing assets, analysing securities and managing a portfolio.

statements.paraphrase: Will gather, organise, combine and make sense of financial, accounting and economic data.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will collect, manage, combine and interpret financial, accounting and economic data.

forBeneficiary.text: To pass, you will gather, organise, combine and make sense of financial, accounting and economic data.

statements.paraphrase: Will carry out simple statistical analyses of financial data in software.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will execute straightforward statistical analyses of financial data with software packages.

forBeneficiary.text: To pass, you will run simple statistical analyses of financial data using software.

statements.paraphrase: Will judge the importance, problems and limits of finance theories and the evidence behind them.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will assess how far finance theories and their evidence matter, and their problems and limits.

forBeneficiary.text: To pass, you will judge how far finance theories and their evidence hold up, and where they fall short.

statements.about: theory and evidence guiding policy and practice
statements.paraphrase: Will show a critical understanding of how theory and evidence in finance can inform policy and practice.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will critically appreciate how finance theory and empirical evidence can guide policy and practice.

forBeneficiary.text: To pass, you will show you understand, critically, how finance theory and evidence can shape policy and practice.

statements.about: finance as a lever for sustainable outcomes
statements.paraphrase: Will understand why finance is a key means of reaching sustainable outcomes for society and the planet.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will understand finance as a key lever for sustainable outcomes for society and the planet.

forBeneficiary.text: To pass, you will understand how finance can drive sustainable outcomes for people and the planet.

statements.about: the effect of fintech on financial services
statements.paraphrase: Will understand how fintech changes financial services through AI, blockchain and digital payments.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will understand the impact of fintech innovations such as AI, blockchain and digital payments on financial services.

forBeneficiary.text: To pass, you will understand how fintech, such as AI, blockchain and digital payments, is changing financial services.

statements.about: summarising and communicating to varied audiences
statements.paraphrase: Will condense financial knowledge and information and convey it well, orally and in writing, to varied audiences.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will distil financial information and communicate it effectively, spoken and written, to diverse audiences.

forBeneficiary.text: To pass, you will boil down financial information and explain it well, in speech and writing, to different audiences.

statements.paraphrase: Will show they can collaborate and lead by working well in finance and cross-disciplinary teams.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will show collaborative and leadership skills in finance and interdisciplinary teams.

forBeneficiary.text: To pass, you will show you can work with others and lead, in finance teams and mixed-discipline teams.

statements.paraphrase: Will show independent thought and critical judgement.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will assert intellectual independence and critical judgement.

forBeneficiary.text: To pass, you will think for yourself and judge critically.

statements.paraphrase: Graduates at the typical level stand out from those at threshold by the breadth and depth of what they know and understand and by clear, critical insight into finance.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates show breadth and depth of knowledge and a clear, critical insight into the discipline, beyond the threshold.

forBeneficiary.text: To go beyond a pass, you will show broad and deep knowledge and a clear, critical view of finance as a discipline.

statements.about: rigorous theory and some specialised topics
statements.paraphrase: Will show a rigorous grasp of the theories, paradigms, methods, concepts and principles of finance, and a strong grasp of some specialised topics.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will show rigorous understanding of finance theory and method and strong understanding of some specialist topics.

forBeneficiary.text: To go beyond a pass, you will show a rigorous grasp of finance theory and method and know some specialist topics well.

statements.about: critical appraisal of sources and their limits
statements.paraphrase: Will have a sophisticated ability to choose many kinds of information, sources, views and knowledge and appraise them critically, specialised or interdisciplinary, recognising their uncertainty, ambiguity and limits.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will select and critically appraise a wide range of sources, specialist or interdisciplinary, and recognise their uncertainty and limits.

forBeneficiary.text: To go beyond a pass, you will choose and critically weigh many kinds of sources and views, and see where they are uncertain or limited.

statements.paraphrase: With some autonomy, will carry out thorough investigation, reading, analysis and research and solve complex finance problems, using a wide range of established methods accurately.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will investigate thoroughly with some autonomy and solve complex finance problems with established methods, accurately.

forBeneficiary.text: To go beyond a pass, you will research thoroughly with some independence and solve complex finance problems using a wide range of methods accurately.

statements.about: synthesis, argument and originality in communication
statements.paraphrase: Will select, evaluate, synthesise, discuss and present information and results with well-supported arguments, interpreting complex ideas thoroughly and showing a high degree of creativity and originality.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will synthesise and present information and results with supported arguments, interpret complex ideas thoroughly and show creativity and originality.

forBeneficiary.text: To go beyond a pass, you will pull information together, argue from evidence, explain complex ideas carefully and show creativity and original thought in your work.

statements.paraphrase: Graduates at the excellent level stand out from those at threshold and typical levels by exceptional knowledge and understanding of finance, well past the typical and past what was taught.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates show exceptional knowledge and understanding of finance, well beyond the typical level and beyond what was taught.

forBeneficiary.text: At the highest level, you will show exceptional knowledge and understanding of finance, going well past what you were taught.

statements.about: exceptional theory and in-depth specialist knowledge
statements.paraphrase: Will show exceptional command of the theories, paradigms, methods, concepts and principles of finance and deep knowledge of several specialised areas.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will show exceptional command of finance theory and method and in-depth knowledge of several specialist areas.

forBeneficiary.text: At the highest level, you will show exceptional command of finance theory and method and know several specialist areas in depth.

statements.paraphrase: Will think independently and carry out thorough, extensive investigation, reading, analysis and research well past the typical range.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will work with intellectual independence and investigate thoroughly and extensively, well beyond the typical range.

forBeneficiary.text: At the highest level, you will think independently and research thoroughly and widely, well beyond what most students do.

statements.paraphrase: Will have an exceptional ability to appraise many sources, views and knowledge critically and a masterly sense of their uncertainty, ambiguity and limits.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will critically appraise a wide range of sources with exceptional skill and show a masterly grasp of their uncertainty and limits.

forBeneficiary.text: At the highest level, you will weigh up a wide range of sources with exceptional skill and show a masterly sense of what they cannot tell you.

statements.paraphrase: Will show exceptional problem-solving and strong decision-making on complex finance problems, working largely autonomously, justifying and evidencing the critical and accurate use of a wide range of established methods.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will solve complex finance problems exceptionally well and largely autonomously, justifying their choice and use of methods critically and accurately.

forBeneficiary.text: At the highest level, you will solve complex finance problems exceptionally well and largely on your own, and justify the methods you chose.

statements.paraphrase: Will proficiently select, evaluate, synthesise, discuss and present views, information and results.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will proficiently select, evaluate, synthesise and present views, information and results.

forBeneficiary.text: At the highest level, you will select, weigh, combine and present views, information and results with real skill.

statements.paraphrase: Will build and present well-supported arguments and show sophisticated perception, critical insight into complex matters and exceptional creativity, flair and originality.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will build supported arguments with sophisticated insight into complex matters and show exceptional creativity and originality.

forBeneficiary.text: At the highest level, you will build strong, evidenced arguments, see deeply into complex matters and show exceptional creativity and originality.
